thread.title: Maryland expands warning to all Clover Hill cheese after listeria outbreak tied to death
thread.title_full: Maryland expands warning to all Clover Hill cheese after listeria outbreak tied to death

author: beaver state news
title: Maryland expands warning to all Clover Hill cheese after listeria outbreak tied to death
text:
Maryland officials expanded a food safety alert on June 17 to include all cheeses produced by Clover Hill Dairy, following a multistate listeria outbreak that has been linked to one death. The advisory now covers every cheese made by the Mechanicsville-based company, regardless of brand name.
Officials said no Clover Hill cheese products should be eaten, sold, or served. This follows the Maryland Department of Health’s decision to broaden its advisory beyond specific products previously identified in the investigation.
Clover Hill Dairy announced it is initiating a voluntary recall covering its entire cheese lineup. In a statement, the company said, “To the best of our knowledge, to date, eight cases of Listeria infections may have been linked to [our] soft cheese, as published by the FDA in cooperation with the Maryland Department of Health.” The statement continued: “Clover Hill Dairy has ceased production and distribution of all cheese products and has initiated a voluntary recall. … Consumers who have purchased recalled Clover Hill Dairy Soft Ricotta/Requeson cheese are urged to return it to the place of purchase in its original packaging for a full refund.”
Health officials reported that whole genome sequencing connected the outbreak strain with nine illnesses across several states. The affected cheeses were sold at Clover Hill’s retail market, farmers markets, and through outside distributors in Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina, New York, New Jersey, and Washington D.C.
The Department of Health has suspended Clover Hill’s operating license due to ongoing public health risks while continuing its investigation. Officials warn that listeria bacteria can survive and grow even under refrigeration and can spread easily on counters or containers. Symptoms may include fever, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting or diarrhea; severe cases can result in stiff necks or confusion and may be fatal—especially for pregnant people, older adults or those with weakened immune systems.
Consumers are advised not only to discard any Clover Hill Dairy cheeses but also any foods prepared with them. Surfaces and utensils that came into contact with these products should be washed and sanitized thoroughly because listeria can persist in kitchen environments. People who develop symptoms after consuming these cheeses are encouraged to contact their healthcare provider.
summary: Maryland officials expanded a food safety alert on June 17 to include all cheeses produced by Clover Hill Dairy, following a multistate listeria outbreak that has been linked to one death. Clover Hill Dairy announced it is initiating a voluntary recall covering its entire cheese lineup.
